title: Recursive Agent Harnesses

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 ('All runs use temperature zero'); gpt-5 is a reasoning model and ignores temperature, so only max_completion_tokens is sent, set generously because subagent outputs and the extraction call are free-form

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: 199 samples drawn from the Oolong-Synthetic validation split, stratified across all 13 context-length buckets (1K to 4M tokens, average 629K tokens per instance); the same 199-sample protocol as the baselines of Cao et al.
task.approximation: RAH is a recursive multi-agent harness: a parent agent writes and executes a script that spawns one full subagent harness per entry (thousands in parallel), each with filesystem and shell tools, and a final GPT-5 answer-extraction call. Nothing of that fits a single chat completion.

items.source: huggingface.co/datasets/oolongbench/oolong-synth (Oolong-Synthetic; the paper attributes the data and the baseline numbers to Cao et al. and Zhang et al.)
items.config_or_split: split validation (1,300 examples, 4.43 GB) - far above the 50 MB download limit, so the rows were not fetched; the 199-sample stratified subset is not enumerated in the paper
items.license: unknown (the dataset card declares no licence)
items.size_limit_note: items.hf is deliberately NOT set. The validation split is 4.43 GB, so a --prepare with a machine-readable hf block starts a download far above the project's 50 MB rule; the hub id is kept under items.hf_paper instead and the runner stops with NEEDS_HUMAN.

placeholders.question: the Oolong question
placeholders.raw_output: the subagent's raw output for that instance

prompt.source_location: Appendix C ('Answer-Extraction Prompt'); Appendices A and B hold the parent and subagent prompts
prompt.verbatim: full for the answer-extraction prompt of Appendix C (the last stage only). The parent and subagent system prompts of Appendices A and B are printed as fragments in the extracted text and are not the stage that produces the score.

output.postprocess: the extraction call returns the bare answer value; a regular-expression parser is the documented fallback (never used on the 199 instances)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Oolong Score = micro-average over the 199 instances of a per-instance score that is exact match for LABEL, COMPARISON, USER and DATE answer types and 0.75^|y - yhat| for NUMERIC answers; deterministic, no model judge (Sec. 4.1)
metric.judge: none for scoring; gpt-5-2025-08-07 is used as a format extractor before scoring, and its prompt is printed (Appendix C)
metric.original_location: Table 1 / Figure 2, row 'RAH, GPT-5 (ours)' (baselines in the same table: full-context 59.22, RLM 64.38, Codex no-retriever 71.75, all measured by Cao et al.)

open_points: harness not released: 'The Recursive Agent Harness implementation and the evaluation and scoring scripts will be released shortly.' Without them the parent/subagent orchestration, the spawning script and the scorer would all have to be re-implemented from the prose, so the number would not be a re-run of the published system.

data over the limit: the Oolong-Synthetic validation split is 4.43 GB (average 629K tokens per instance, up to 4M), far above the 50 MB rule, and the 199-instance stratified subset is not enumerated. items.hf is therefore left unset on purpose so that --prepare cannot start the download; a human has to decide how to obtain and subset the rows.
architecture: thousands of parallel subagent harnesses with filesystem and shell access per instance, plus a separate extraction call, is outside the Tier B runner and would need its own sandbox.
cost: 199 instances at an average of 629K context tokens spread over a parent plus many subagents runs into the high hundreds of dollars even before retries - an explicit budget decision.
notes: The only piece of this paper that is fully specified and cheap is the answer-extraction stage of Appendix C, and it presupposes subagent outputs to extract from. The Claude Sonnet 4.5 configuration in the same table (89.77) is out of scope.
